title: Offer-to-Impact 7-day Sprint Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This working checklist captures a condensed, people-ops-led 7-day plan to move an accepted offer to first measurable impact. It blends preboarding, minimal friction access, focused technical ramp, and a calibrated interview-feedback loop to validate expectations. Use this as a tactical runbook for IC hires across platform/product/infra to reduce day-0 cognitive load and accelerate contributor value by week 2.

Context + constraints:
- For hires with technical responsibilities (engineer, SRE, solutions eng).
- Designed for roles that already have a buddy or mentor assigned.
- Assumes access provisioning pipeline (IT/SSO/Kickstart) takes up to 48 hours in some regions.
- This is intentionally prescriptive—follow steps in order but mark blockers in the blockers section and escalate to people-ops.

Quick owner map (who does what):
- Hiring manager: craft first-week mini-scope, prioritize 1-2 nonblocking tasks, own schedule for the week.
- Buddy/Mentor: daily 30m sync, hands-on pairing, codebase walkthrough.
- People Ops: coordinate preboarding, equipment, payroll, benefits orientation, runbook hygiene.
- IT/Security: ensure SSO, device enrollment, VPN, and secrets access (where applicable).
- Eng Ops: repo access, CI runner tokens, infra sandbox.

Preboarding (Offer accepted to Day 0) — checklist items:
- Confirm start date and timezone, send welcome email with agenda (people-ops).
- Equipment order placed and tracked (laptop + power + peripherals).
- Invite to #new-joiner-orbit Slack and team channel; create calendar blocks for day 1-3 (people-ops + manager).
- Share the one-pager: team context, mission, key services, immediate goals, and where to be productive in first 7 days (manager).
- Assign buddy and set expectation: daily 30m pairing and lunchtime intro (manager).
- Create access ticket template prefilled with role and list of repos/services needed (eng-ops).
- Security briefing doc link + NDA confirmations (security).

Day 0 (first working day) — minimal friction goals:
- 09:00–09:30 Welcome + orientation (people-ops): payroll, benefits, Slack/KV hygiene.
- 10:00–11:30 Team kickoff + 1:1 with manager: set the 7-day compact and agree on three success signals.
- 13:00–16:00 Environment setup block: device enrollment, git ssh keys, repo clones, basic smoke run (buddy + eng-ops).
- 16:00–16:30 Quick demo: local dev loop working example (buddy).
- Deliverable by EOD: comment on the onboarding tracker with “env ready / blockers list”.

Day 1–2 — bootstrapping real work:
- Provide a single scoped starter ticket (manager): non-critical bug or doc update that exercises codepath + CI.
- Pair session 2–3x 45m to onboard codebase mental model (buddy).
- Short product orientation: architecture diagram, ownership map, incident runbook overview.
- Security/Compliance short read + quiz (if role requires handling PII or customer data).
- Check: repo CI passes locally and remote PR created against starter ticket.

Day 3–4 — iterative context and small wins:
- Ramp ticket: complete code + tests + CI green + 1 reviewer prompt (manager + buddy).
- Short retro with manager: what was unclear, what wasted time, where to improve.
- Introduce cross-team stakeholders and brief owners (30m each) for services the hire will touch.

Day 5–7 — reliability and momentum:
- Deliver second scoped task that touches infra/service integration.
- Shadow an oncall rotation or postmortem read if relevant (SRE hires).
- Ownership checkpoint: share a 1-page plan for next 30 days (what to own, dependencies, learning gaps).
- Schedule initial 30/60/90 expectations sync with manager and buddy.

Interview-rubric tie-in (closing the loop):
- Within first 7 days manager must flag whether the candidate met the expected baseline used during interview.
- If mismatch, create an evidence log using the rubric categories: technical competency, problem decomposition, communication, delivery, and culture fit. Attach sample artifacts (PRs, pairing notes) and tag people-ops for potential remediation plan.
- Use a lightweight rating: Met / Partially met / Not met. For Partially met or Not met, follow up with a 14-day coaching plan.

People-ops templates (copy + paste snippets):
- Welcome email subject: Welcome to Redwood — Start date, first steps + essential links.
- Starter ticket template: summary, acceptance criteria, dev notes, how to run locally, reviewer suggestions.
- Access ticket checklist: SSO, GitHub org, primary repo, CI runner, registry read, k8s dev namespace, secrets read (if applicable).

Blockers & escalation guide:
- If equipment delayed beyond Day 1: allocate cloud dev sandbox + temporary device stipend.
- If access not provisioned by EOD Day 1: people-ops alerts IT+eng-ops; candidate given explicit ETA and interim tasks (reading, design doc prep).
- If candidate environment broken CI on Day 3: buddy creates a reproducible issue thread and flags manager for prioritized pairing.

Success signals (used to judge first-week effectiveness):
- Environment is reproducible and documented in onboarding tracker.
- Two PRs submitted with green CI and 1 reviewer feedback.
- Candidate delivered a clear 1-page plan for first 30 days.
- Manager and buddy comfortable with the trainee’s current trajectory (qualitative).

Lightweight measurement & feedback loop:
- People-ops runs a brief pulse survey on Day 7 covering: clarity of role, blockers, relationship with buddy, and perceived ramp speed.
- Manager files a short note in the hiring folder summarizing fit and any remediation.

Notes to future editors / TODOs:
- Add region-specific provisioning times for APAC + EMEA (we still see longer SSO delays).
- Consider auto-generating starter ticket from role templates in the new-hire pipeline.
- Build a one-click checklist in the onboarding tracker that wires up all calendar invites and access tickets.

Quick links:
- Onboarding tracker: drive:hr/onboarding-tracker (internal)
- Starter ticket templates: github:org/onboarding-templates
- New-joiner Slack: #new-joiner-orbit
- Security onboarding: confluence:security/new-hire-brief

Last updated notes:
- 2026-03-05: switched to 7-day compact (previously 10-day), tightened deliverable expectations and added interview-rubric tie-in.

— end of working draft —

Small-print: This doc is intentionally pragmatic and should be used alongside role-specific onboarding artifacts (SRE, infra, product) that expand the starter ticket and compliance training. If you adapt this for a non-technical hire, remove the CI/dev environment steps and replace with product/ops shadowing milestones.
